content: {"summary":"The payments‑db volume is >85% full and PostgreSQL is about to panic. The only safe, immediate way to buy a few minutes is to delete the 10 GB ballast file on the volume. The underlying problem is WAL accumulation, most commonly caused by a replication slot that is no longer advancing, which keeps old WAL segments on disk.","likely_cause":"WAL buildup due to an inactive replication slot (or other WAL holder) filling the volume","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The ballast file is the only safe deletable file on the volume.","evidence_ids":["RB-007#5"],"quote":"This is the only file on that volume you may delete."},{"text":"A replication slot not advancing can cause WAL to fill the disk.","evidence_ids":["RB-007#1"],"quote":"A replication slot is not advancing."},{"text":"Disk alerts show usage above 85% and 95% on the PostgreSQL data volume.","evidence_ids":["RB-007#3"],"quote":"Disk alert on payments-db-01 for `/var/lib/postgresql` above 85%, then 95%."}],"next_checks":["Run `SELECT slot_name, active, wal_status, pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)) FROM pg_replication_slots;` to identify any inactive slot holding large WAL.","Check `pg_stat_archiver` for recent failures that might be preventing WAL removal.","Verify current disk usage with `du -sh /var/lib/postgresql/16/main/pg_wal` after deleting the ballast file.","If a slot is confirmed stuck, obtain DBA approval and consider `pg_drop_replication_slot` for the offending slot.","Request an online volume expansion in the cloud console while performing the above steps."]}
